title: Dedicated capacity forecasting and fast-fail autoscale strategy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: define and deliver a quarterly roadmap slice that reduces overprovision costs on Dedicated while preserving latency SLAs. This ticket covers the product plan, acceptance criteria, rollout gating, and OKR alignment for two complementary initiatives: (1) Forecast-driven reservation hedging (improve capacity forecasts and reserve shorter burst increments) and (2) Fast-fail autoscale (rapid reactive scale with conservative hedging to avoid prolonged over-commit). The intent is to reduce committed but unused GPU-hours, improve cost predictability for customers, and ensure fail-safe behavior under sudden load spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Forecasting model integrated into capacity planner: daily predicted capacity demand with 7/30-day windows produced and visible in Console
Autoscale fast-fail path implemented: scale-up attempts that cannot be fulfilled within the safety window trigger deterministic fallback routing to pre-approved model variants or lower-rep tiers
SLO guardrails in place: no more than 0.5% increase in request error-rate during scale events and P95 latency impact <= 10% for impacted routes
Cost telemetry and billing reconciliation: per-customer delta of committed vs. used GPU-hours tracked and surfaced; dashboards for finance and customer success
Rollout plan documented and tested with two pilot customers (internal ops + one external beta) and rollback criteria defined
success_metrics: 25% reduction in average daily committed-but-unused GPU-hours for pilot group within first 30 days
>=90% of scale-up attempts in the fast-fail path resolve to a valid fallback within 15s
<1% customer-facing incidents attributed to autoscale during pilot
Finance: demonstrable reduction in monthly hedging reserve by pilot customers without SLA violations

decision_log: 2026-02-16: Chosen approach — hybrid: predictive hedging for scheduled demand windows + fast-fail reactive path for sudden spikes. Rationale: forecasting alone leaves edge spikes exposed; purely reactive autoscale risks cost spikes.
2026-02-18: Fallback policies will be opt-in per-customer with recommended defaults. Customers can specify fallback model families or a tiered degradation policy.
2026-02-20: Canary window set to 2 weeks for internal alpha, followed by 4-week external beta with one reference customer. Canaries gated on telemetry thresholds (error rate, latency, cost delta).
2026-02-21: Decided not to bundle this release with full RBAC changes; separate release to avoid scope creep. Security review flagged as not required for this roadmap slice.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Design & infra prep (2 weeks): finalize API for fallback policies, add telemetry hooks, define SLOs
Phase 1 — Internal alpha (2 weeks): enable for internal ops namespace, run synthetic and replay traffic, validate fallback behavior
Phase 2 — External beta (4 weeks): enable for two pilot customers with clear billing opt-in; CS and account owners on-call
Phase 3 — Gradual GA (4 weeks): tiered enablement by customer size with automated recommendations from Console; enable billing reconciliation
Rollback criteria: sustained >1% customer errors attributed to autoscale for >1h, or >15% unexpected cost delta for pilot customers
risks_mitigation: Risk: Forecast inaccuracies lead to underprovisioning. Mitigation: conservative hedging buffer, rapid fallback routing, and automated escalation to on-call SREs.
Risk: Fallback routing causes degraded output quality. Mitigation: require customer-specified fallback families and include quality regression alerts in onboarding
Risk: Billing disputes from short-burst reservations. Mitigation: clear opt-in billing language, pre-beta finance reconciliation, and per-customer dashboards
Risk: SLA breach during scale events. Mitigation: limit fast-fail aggressive scaling to non-critical routes until beta passes
